age.evidence: A total of 96 male and female adult Wistar rats (Rattus norvegicus, 60 days old

sex.evidence: male n = 48, mean weight 435 g (s.d. 21.1), females n = 48, mean weight 260 g (s.d. 25.4)

dosing.doses_raw: 2 mL/kg; DMT 2.72 mg/kg, harmine 3.98 mg/kg, harmaline 0.20 mg/kg, tetrahydroharmine 3.72 mg/kg (~10.62 mg/kg total alkaloids)
dosing.evidence: rats were given an intragastric dose of Ayahuasca (2 mL/kg) or filtered water through intragastric gavage at the same volume (2 mL/kg). (Ayahuasca is an aqueous brew; filtered water was the control; numeric dose listed is DMT content)

group_housing.evidence: Animals were maintained in same-sex groups of four per cage throughout the experiment

day_night_flipped.evidence: Animals were kept in a 12-h light-dark cycle at 22 ± 1 °C (direction not specified)

enrichment_housing.evidence: Only 'socially enriched housing conditions' mentioned; no enrichment items described

assays.assay_name: Relapse-like ethanol consumption (3-bottle choice, home cage)
assays.assay_description: Home-cage voluntary 3-bottle choice (water, 15% and 30% ethanol) during a 9-day relapse phase after single Ayahuasca/water gavage; cage-level intake normalised to body weight (g/kg/day, mL/kg/day); establishment-phase intake analysed as pre-treatment baseline.

application_type.evidence: rats were given an intragastric dose of Ayahuasca (2 mL/kg) or filtered water through intragastric gavage

setup_restrain.evidence: renewed free access to 15% and 30% ethanol for 9 consecutive days (home cage)

food_restriction.evidence: continuous, ad libitum access to food, filtered water, and two additional bottles

water_restriction.evidence: had ad libitum access to filtered water and regular chow

time_to_assay.evidence: The day after the end of the alcohol withdrawal phase, rats were given an intragastric dose of Ayahuasca... Following the 9 days of alcohol withdrawal, a relapse phase consisting of renewed free access... (days 45-53)

sample_size.evidence: N = 12 animals/group for panels A and C; three-way RM ANOVA F(2,88), Sex×Treatment F(1,44) (alcohol-exposed groups only)

outcomes.summary: A single Ayahuasca dose reduced relapse-like ethanol intake in a sex- and concentration-dependent manner: in males both 15% and 30% ethanol intake decreased, in females only 30% ethanol intake decreased; water intake unaffected.
outcomes.statistics: Bottle × Sex × Treatment F(2,88)=25.22, P<0.0001; Bottle × Sex F(2,88)=29.42, P<0.0001; Bottle × Treatment F(2,88)=64.50, P<0.0001; Sex × Treatment F(1,44)=2.042, P=0.1600; males 15% P<0.0001, males 30% P<0.0001, females 30% P<0.0001, females 15% P>0.9999
outcomes.evidence: In males, Ayahuasca significantly reduced consumption of both the 15% ethanol solution (P <0.0001) and the 30% ethanol solution (P < 0.0001). In females, Ayahuasca significantly reduced 30% ethanol consumption (P < 0.0001), whereas 15% ethanol consumption did not differ between treatment groups (P >0.9999).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Consumption of water, 15% ethanol, and 30% ethanol solutions during the relapse phase

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: The original daily alcohol-consumption data were lost due to a hardware malfunction, preventing analysis of the temporal dynamics of relapse drinking

B4_ethological.evidence: Fluid intake volume per cage; not a scored ethological act

B5_social.evidence: Assay measures fluid consumption, no social construct

E1_environment_type.evidence: because ethanol solutions were provided at the cage level

E6_spatial.evidence: standard home cage; no compartments described

E7_social_context.evidence: Animals were maintained in same-sex groups of four per cage throughout the experiment

E8_food_water.evidence: continuous, ad libitum access to food, filtered water, and two additional bottles

D1_continuity.evidence: relapse phase consisting of renewed free access to 15% and 30% ethanol for 9 consecutive days (intake measured repeatedly; reported as averages)

D2_session_duration.evidence: continuous free access to bottles for 9 consecutive days

D3_recording_days.evidence: renewed free access to 15% and 30% ethanol for 9 consecutive days

D4_baseline.evidence: To characterize baseline alcohol preference before treatment administration, fluid consumption during the establishment phase was analyzed

D5_followup.evidence: Relapse intake recorded across 9 days following the single Ayahuasca administration (>=24 h post-dose)

assays.assay_description: 5-min free exploration of plus maze (two open 50×10 cm, two closed 50×10×40 cm arms, red light); time in open arms recorded; no prior habituation; blinded experimenter.

setup_habituation.evidence: no prior habituation to the EPM apparatus was performed

setup_restrain.evidence: was allowed to freely explore the apparatus for 5 min

food_restriction.evidence: standard EPM apparatus; no food in apparatus

water_restriction.evidence: standard EPM apparatus; no water in apparatus

time_to_assay.evidence: Ayahuasca on day 45; behavioral assessments (days 56-60); exact EPM day not stated

sample_size.evidence: Fig. 3A, N = 12/group, except Male Alcohol/Water N = 11 due to one excluded value

outcomes.summary: Alcohol reduced open-arm time in water-treated rats of both sexes; Ayahuasca increased open-arm time in alcohol-exposed males and females, reversing anxiety-like behaviour.
outcomes.statistics: Treatment × Sex × Alcohol F(1,87)=1.668, P=0.2000; Treatment × Alcohol F(1,87)=8.019, P=0.0058; alcohol-exposed males P<0.0001, females P=0.0032
outcomes.evidence: Ayahuasca significantly increased open-arm exploration in alcohol-exposed males (P < 0.0001) and females (P = 0.0032) compared with their respective water-treated alcohol-exposed groups

B1_num_measures.evidence: The total time spent (seconds) in the open arms was recorded for 5 min

B4_ethological.evidence: time in zone is a spatial measure

E1_environment_type.evidence: plus-shaped apparatus with two open and two closed arms

E2_shelter.evidence: EPM closed arms are not a shelter per rubric

E6_spatial.evidence: EPM scored as single space per rubric

E7_social_context.evidence: Each rat was placed on the central platform

D1_continuity.evidence: allowed to freely explore the apparatus for 5 min

D5_followup.evidence: Ayahuasca on day 45; behavioral assessments (days 56-60) — >=24 h after dosing

assays.assay_description: 5-min exploration of 40×60 cm arena (50 cm walls) with floor divided into nine squares; square crossings (reported) and rearing (recorded per methods, not reported in results).

setup_restrain.evidence: allowed to freely explore the arena for 5 min

time_to_assay.evidence: Ayahuasca on day 45; behavioral assessments (days 56-60); exact OFT day not stated

sample_size.evidence: For Fig. 3B, N = 12/group, except Male Control/Water N = 11 due to one excluded value and Male Alcohol/Water N = 11 due to one missing value

outcomes.summary: Main effects of Treatment and Sex on square crossings, but no interactions and no significant pairwise differences; limited evidence of locomotor change.
outcomes.evidence: Post hoc comparisons did not identify significant pairwise differences between groups (all P ≥ 0.0755)

B1_num_measures.evidence: Only 'Total crossings in the Open Field Test' reported (Fig. 3B); rearing recorded but not reported as a result

B4_ethological.evidence: crossings are a locomotor measure; rearing not reported

E3_bedding.evidence: floor divided by black lines into nine squares; no bedding mentioned

E7_social_context.evidence: Each rat was placed in the back left corner

D1_continuity.evidence: allowed to freely explore the arena for 5 min

D5_followup.evidence: behavioral assessments (days 56-60), >=11 days after dosing on day 45

assays.assay_description: Day 58: 5-min habituation in 40×60 cm wooden box, then 2 mL 10% sucrose applied to the back and grooming time recorded for 5 min.

setup_habituation.evidence: After 5 min of habituation, rats were removed from the apparatus and 2 mL of a 10% sucrose solution was applied

setup_restrain.evidence: rats were returned to the apparatus for an additional 5 min

time_to_assay.evidence: The splash test was carried out on day 58; Ayahuasca on day 45

sample_size.evidence: For Fig. 3C, N = 12/group, except Male Control/Ayahuasca N = 11 due to one excluded value and Male Alcohol/Water N = 8 due to three excluded values and one missing value

outcomes.summary: Alcohol reduced grooming in water-treated rats of both sexes; Ayahuasca increased grooming in alcohol-exposed males and females.
outcomes.statistics: Treatment × Sex × Alcohol F(1,83)=0.1472, P=0.7022; Treatment × Alcohol F(1,83)=29.12, P<0.0001; alcohol-exposed males P=0.0015, females P<0.0001
outcomes.evidence: Ayahuasca significantly increased grooming behavior in alcohol-exposed males (P =0.0015) and females (P <0.0001) compared with their respective water-treated alcohol-exposed groups

B1_num_measures.evidence: The time spent grooming (seconds) was used as a measure

E7_social_context.evidence: rats were returned to the apparatus

D1_continuity.evidence: returned to the apparatus for an additional 5 min

D4_baseline.evidence: habituation without data collection; no pre-drug baseline

D5_followup.evidence: day 58, 13 days after Ayahuasca on day 45

assays.assay_description: Two-day protocol: 15-min pre-swim (day 59) and 5-min test (day 60) in Plexiglas cylinder (50 cm × 25 cm, 23 °C); immobility and climbing scored manually; only climbing reported in results.

setup_habituation.evidence: On the first day (training phase), rats were placed in a transparent Plexiglas cylinder ... for 15 min

setup_restrain.evidence: FST cylinder (rubric classifies FST as restrained)

water_restriction.evidence: water is swim medium, not drinking source

time_to_assay.evidence: The FST was performed over two days, on days 59 and 60 (test day 60); Ayahuasca on day 45

sample_size.evidence: For Fig. 3D, N = 12/group, except Male Control/Water N = 11 due to one excluded value, Male Control/Ayahuasca N = 10 due to two excluded values, and Male Alcohol/Water N = 11 due to one excluded value

outcomes.summary: Alcohol reduced climbing in water-treated males and females; Ayahuasca increased climbing only in alcohol-exposed females.
outcomes.statistics: Treatment × Sex × Alcohol F(1,84)=0.01211, P=0.9126; Treatment × Alcohol F(1,84)=8.094, P=0.0056; Sex × Alcohol F(1,84)=7.057, P=0.0094; alcohol-exposed females P=0.0357
outcomes.evidence: Ayahuasca increased climbing behavior in alcohol-exposed females compared with water-treated alcohol-exposed females (P = 0.0357)

B1_num_measures.evidence: Results report only 'Climbing behavior in the Forced Swim Test' (Fig. 3D); immobility measured per methods but not reported

B4_ethological.evidence: FST behaviours not ethological per rubric

E1_environment_type.evidence: transparent Plexiglas cylinder (height: 50 cm, diameter: 25 cm)

E7_social_context.evidence: rats were placed in a transparent Plexiglas cylinder

D1_continuity.evidence: Only test-phase (day 60, 5 min) data reported; training-phase data not reported

D2_session_duration.evidence: On the second day (test phase), rats were placed again in the same cylinder for 5 min

D5_followup.evidence: day 60, 15 days after Ayahuasca on day 45

judge_notes: All three candidates identified the same five assays (relapse drinking, EPM, OFT, splash, FST); biochemical analyses (monoamines, BDNF, oxidative stress) excluded as ex vivo.

D5_followup set to Yes for all assays, overriding qwen/gemma: all behaviour was recorded >=24 h after the single dose (EPM/OFT/splash/FST on days 56-60 vs dosing day 45; relapse intake over 9 days post-dose).
Relapse D4 baseline = Yes (modal): establishment-phase intake analysed as pre-treatment baseline. B1 corrected to score 1 (gemma gave 2 for '2-3'). B4 = No (modal).
Relapse sample size corrected to 48 (24M/24F): only alcohol-exposed groups drank ethanol in relapse (Sex×Treatment df 1,44); candidates reported 96.
Relapse D1 kept at modal 'Multiple discrete sessions' despite D2/D6 reflecting continuous 24-h access; intake was cage-level and daily data were lost.
OFT and FST B1 set to 1 measure (overriding modal 2-3): results report only crossings (OFT) and only climbing (FST); rearing/immobility were recorded per methods but not reported as results.

FST D1/D3 set to single session/1 day: training-phase data not reported; consistent with modal D2 (<15 min) which counted only the 5-min test. FST setup_habituation = yes (15-min pre-swim without data) and setup_restrain = yes per rubric.
FST sex_dependent = yes: Ayahuasca effect significant only in females.
Sample sizes per test computed from Fig. 3 legend exclusions (all exclusions in males).
Vehicle set to 'water' (filtered water control; Ayahuasca is an aqueous brew); dose array lists DMT content (2.72 mg/kg), with full alkaloid composition in doses_raw.
